newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico, El Salvador sign accords to boost ties.
newsitem.headline: Mexico, El Salvador sign accords to boost ties.

text.p: Mexico and El Salvador signed several accords to strengthen bilateral ties on Wednesday at the start of a state visit of the Central American nation's President Armando Calderon Sol.
"We want to be partners for development," Calderon Sol said during a ceremony at the Mexican president's official residence of Los Pinos.

Each side also pledged to strengthen trade ties, something Central American countries have been eager to do with Mexico since it signed its own free-trade pact with the United States and Canada in 1994.
"We want to advance free trade between Mexico, El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras," said Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo at the official reception.
Both sides signed an extradition treaty, one on mutual legal assistance, and several on education cooperation and transfer of technology.
One treaty will allow about 1,000 Salvadorean products to be imported into Mexico that were previously restricted.
Calderon's visit is scheduled to last four days, two of which will be spent in the northern industrial city of Monterrey.
